methodology: The original research topic and the generated technical specification were decomposed into atomic units by identifying individual requirements, features, behaviors, and constraints. Each atomic unit is designed to be independent, self-contained, technically specific, unambiguous, and implementable as a single requirement. This ensures a granular comparison between the two information sources.
mindtraced_atomic_units: Inputs: x, y from motor, clk, synchronous active-low resetn.
When resetn is low, FSM is in state A.
When resetn de-asserts, f = 1 for one clock cycle.
If x sequence is 1, 0, 1, then g = 1 on the following clock cycle.
While g = 1, FSM monitors y input for max 2 clock cycles.
If y = 1 within 2 cycles, g remains 1 until resetn.
If y != 1 within 2 cycles, g = 0 until resetn.
When resetn asserts, FSM returns to state A, f and g are 0.
spec_atomic_units: Module has inputs clk, resetn, x, y and outputs f, g.
f is asserted for one clock cycle after resetn is de-asserted.
Combinational logic detects de-assertion of resetn and generates a single-cycle pulse for f.
Sequence Detection: x must produce the sequence 1, 0, 1 in three successive clock cycles.
Sequence detection requires storing the previous two values of x (x_prev1, x_prev2).
g is set to 1 on the clock cycle following the 1,0,1 x sequence.
y Input Monitoring: After the sequence 1, 0, 1 is detected, y is monitored for at most two clock cycles.
If y is 1 within these two cycles, g remains permanently at 1 (until reset).
If y is not 1 within these two cycles, g is set to 0 permanently (until reset).
Logic to maintain the permanent state of g (either 1 or 0) until reset.
resetn has priority and forces the FSM to a known state (state A) when asserted low.
The detection of the x sequence (1, 0, 1) requires monitoring x for three clock cycles.
The monitoring of y occurs for a maximum of two clock cycles after g becomes 1.
The outputs f and g are updated synchronously with the rising edge of clk.
